newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Brussels bourse to outperform others -van Lanschot.
newsitem.headline: Brussels bourse to outperform others -van Lanschot.

text.p: The Brussels bourse is likely to outperform most of its surrounding markets in the year ahead, Dutch brokerage van Lanschot Bankiers NV said in a report on Belgian equities released on Thursday.

Van Lanschot said it expected the Bel-20 index to rise 13 percent to 2,825 points in the year to July 14, 1998, compared with a rise of seven percent in the Dutch index, 10 percent in Germany's DAX, 11 percent in France's CAC-40 and eight percent in Britain's FTSE-100.
Van Lanschot took as its base for calculations a Bel-20 index level of 2,500 points. The index was at 2,581.76 points in late trade on Thursday.

Van Lanschot said that from a historical point of view, Brussels was not a leading performer but just in the middle bracket. "Now it seems acceptable to asssume that this will change," van Lanschot said.
It said the Brussels bourse was gradually getting mature, noting its market capitalisation had doubled to more than 5,000 billion francs in the past two and a half years.
It said the economic picture in Belgium was improving and the relative bourse rating was modest.
The risk premium on shares -- the earnings yield on the Bel-20 minus the yield on 10-year state bonds -- was still high compared with other countries, it said.
Van Lanschot named Fortis AG, Barco, Colruyt, Electrabel and Solvay as its favourites for the financials, technology, retail, utilities and basic industries sectors respectively.
